recommendations: Run m01 to m09 in outline order, playlist numbers 28 to 36, straight after e12 (27). One course for Standard 1 and Standard 2.

Joins: m01 opens on e12's final frame exactly (the swing tag with a coded +3%, grey chip 'Earning money: done', chips 'Next: prices go up too' and '?'); the e12 to m01 join is confirmed (ruling 87's provisional mark can be lifted). Each later video opens on the previous video's final frame. m09 hands to math-s11-a01 (provisional until a01 is designed).
Order fix inside the strand (audit N4): m01 opens as a callback to e03 and e10 percentages and does not reteach 'a percentage of an amount'.

Reverse percentages (÷ the multiplier) are taught once, in m02, where GST needs them (÷ 1.1); m01 stays forward only. This keeps m01 to one idea family (multipliers, percentage change, profit and loss).

Money figures (rulings 5 and 32): NSW motor vehicle stamp duty 2026-27 ($3 per $100 or part to $45,000; $1,350 plus $5 per $100 or part above; Revenue NSW, Codex confirms); petrol about $2.25 a litre (ruling 47, NRMA 9 Nov 2026); electricity about 33c/kWh (ruling 47, AER default market offer 2026-27); every other fee, premium, tariff and price is labelled 'example' on screen and Codex finds a dated NSW source near it or reports it. BNPL rules: ASIC Information Sheet 285 (regulated as credit from 10 June 2025), Moneysmart BNPL page (as cited in math-s12-i12). VAT and overseas GST rates (UK 20%, New Zealand 15%): Codex confirms against the governments' pages. Each video says once that prices, fees and rates change.

Strand colour roles (fixed m01 to m06): starting amount, cash price or price before tax blue; percentage, multiplier or rate amber; amount after the change, total or price including tax teal; extra cost (fees, GST component, loss, the cost of a plan above cash) violet; answer green; mistake red. Budget colour roles (m07 to m09): income teal; fixed costs blue; variable essentials olive; discretionary violet; surplus green; deficit red outline (never a crossed slip).

Recurring models introduced once: the multiplier (m01), the parts bar 100 + r (m02), the payment timeline (m03, kit PeriodTimeline), the 'every dollar that leaves your hand' total column (m04), the per-$100 block counter (m05), the inputs-in-cells model sheet (m06, reused m08), the bill = supply charge + usage strip (m07), the times-per-year column (m08), the fund gauge (m09).

Memory aids introduced once: m01 'Up r%: × (1 + r%). Down r%: × (1 − r%). Divide by where you started.'; m02 'GST is 1 part in 11.'; m03 'Free only while every payment is on time.'; m04 'Add every dollar, then compare totals.'; m05 'Drive-away = price + duty + rego + green slip + transfer.'; m06 'Inputs in cells; cost per km = yearly cost ÷ km.'; m07 'Bill = days × supply + units × rate.'; m08 'One period, then subtract: amount × times a year ÷ 52.'; m09 'Budget, save first, keep a fund, check monthly.'

Everyday anchors (no people, hands or faces): sneakers with a swing tag and a phone plan (m01); a supermarket basket and an overseas hoodie (m02); headphones and a t-shirt (m03); a television and a broken fridge (m04); e02's red hatchback at the car yard ($14,990) through m05 and m06; the house meters (m07); a first-job weekly budget on a phone (m08); the car on the hoist with a $2,000 repair (m09; Year 12 i18 reuses the hoist with $6,000).
Pace flags: m01, m05 and m07 are full (about 9 minutes); m02 and m03 lighter. No split proposed.

Header strip (owner rule of 23 Nov: no course labels or module numbers on screen): the m-strand designs show the focus area only, 'MANAGING MONEY'. Existing f, l and e designs show 'MATHEMATICS STANDARD · ...'; root rules whether to align them (open question in the status file).

entries.mainLearnerQuestion: How do percentage increases and decreases set prices, profit and loss?

syllabusActions.text: Apply percentage increase and decrease to determine the cost of goods, and profit and loss

entries.startBoundary: math-s11-e12 final frame: swing tag with coded +3%, grey chip 'Earning money: done', chips 'Next: prices go up too', '?'
entries.stopBoundary: Multipliers for increase and decrease; two changes in a row multiply; percentage change from the starting amount; cost price, selling price, profit or loss and percentage profit or loss on the cost price. Not: reverse percentages (m02), GST (m02), compound growth (Year 12).

entries.mainLearnerQuestion: How do we add or remove GST, and how does VAT work overseas?

syllabusActions.text: Calculate the goods and service tax (GST) or value-added tax (VAT) when purchasing goods and services in Australia and internationally
syllabusActions.siteGap: GST is taught in both directions (managing-money/lesson01). VAT and international purchases are not taught.

syllabusActions.text: Solve problems involving GST or VAT
syllabusActions.siteGap: GST problems are taught; VAT problems are not.

entries.startBoundary: math-s11-m01 final frame: grocery basket with a coded receipt (five items, total $20.30, 'includes GST ?')
entries.stopBoundary: GST 10% on most goods and services, GST-free basics; adding GST (× 1.1), GST on a pre-GST price (× 0.1), removing GST (÷ 1.1, the reverse of a percentage increase), the GST in a GST-inclusive price (÷ 11, one part in eleven); a receipt with GST-free and taxable items; VAT overseas (UK 20%, New Zealand GST 15%) by the same parts idea. Not: currency conversion (prices stay in the local currency), business input tax credits, the tourist refund scheme.
entries.anchors: supermarket basket (ms12-grocery-basket-v1.png) and receipt; a tradesperson's quote; a hoodie bought in London (travel suitcase ma12-travel-suitcase-v1.png)

entries.mainLearnerQuestion: What does buy now, pay later really cost?

syllabusActions.text: Examine payment options involving buy now, pay later and analyse the costs associated with these schemes for purchasing goods

entries.startBoundary: math-s11-m02 final frame: headphones (ma12-headphones-v1.png) with the swing tag '$480', card 'or 4 payments of $120', chips 'Next: buy now, pay later', '?'
entries.stopBoundary: How a pay-in-4 plan works (first payment today, then every two weeks); who pays for 'free' (the shop pays the provider); account fees and late fees; total cost and the extra as a percentage of the price; why a flat fee bites a small purchase harder; several plans at once against a fortnight's spare money; since June 2025 a credit licence and checks. Not: buying on terms or comparing methods (m04); loans and interest (Year 12 i12).
entries.nextHandoff: math-s11-m04 (the television, $1,600, four ways to pay)

entries.mainLearnerQuestion: What does buying on terms cost, and which way of paying suits a purchase?

syllabusActions.text: Calculate the cost of buying on terms that involve paying an initial deposit and making regular repayments
Compare the total cost of using different methods of purchasing goods and justify which method of purchasing is best suited to a given context

entries.startBoundary: math-s11-m03 final frame: television (ms12-television-v1.png) with a coded tag '$1600' and an options card 'cash · lay-by · buy now, pay later · terms', chips 'Next: buying on terms', '?'
entries.stopBoundary: Terms: deposit + repayments × number; extra = total − cash price, as a percentage of the cash price; four methods totalled the same way and ranked; justification by three questions (cash now? every repayment affordable? how urgent?). Not: credit cards and loans with interest rates (Year 12).

entries.mainLearnerQuestion: What does it really cost to buy a car and get it on the road?

syllabusActions.text: Calculate the cost of purchasing a vehicle by considering the purchase price or loan repayments, registration, compulsory and non-compulsory third-party insurance, comprehensive insurance and stamp duty at current rates

entries.startBoundary: math-s11-m04 final frame: red hatchback (ma12-used-hatchback-v1.png) with the windscreen card '$14 990', chips 'drive-away price?', 'Next: buying a car', '?'
entries.stopBoundary: Stamp duty from the current NSW table ($3 per $100 or part; above $45,000 the excess at $5), registration, CTP green slip (compulsory, injury to people), third-party property (optional), comprehensive (optional, your own car too), the excess; on-road cost; buying with a loan (repayments from the lender's calculator, total paid). Not: yearly running costs (m06); interest calculations (Year 12).
entries.nextHandoff: math-s11-m06 (the hatchback with 'drive-away $16 645' and 'every year after?')

entries.mainLearnerQuestion: What does a car cost to run each year, and how does a spreadsheet track it?

syllabusActions.text: Examine the ongoing costs of a vehicle

entries.startBoundary: math-s11-m05 final frame: the hatchback with 'drive-away $16 645' stamped and chips 'every year after?', 'Next: running costs', '?'

entries.mainLearnerQuestion: How do we build a personal budget, on paper and in a spreadsheet?

syllabusActions.text: Prepare a personal budget for a given income, considering fixed and discretionary spending
Use a spreadsheet to model personal and household budgets

entries.stopBoundary: Net income; fixed, variable essential and discretionary spending; converting every amount to one period (amount × times a year ÷ 52); surplus or deficit; savings rate; a spreadsheet model with a times-per-year column; a household budget as the same sheet with shared rows split. entries.mainLearnerQuestion: How do saving, an emergency fund and tracking spending protect us from money trouble?

syllabusActions.text: Examine budgeting, saving, establishing an emergency fund with 3 to 6 months of living expenses, and monitoring spending as strategies designed to minimise financial problems

siteSources: year11/managing-money/lesson06.sa.html (cards 2 to 4; WE2 to WE4; SAQ 2, 3)
entries.startBoundary: math-s11-m08 final frame: the budget phone 'surplus $233 a week' and the car on the hoist (ms12-car-hoist-v1.png) with '$2000 repair?', chips 'Next: an emergency fund', '?'
entries.stopBoundary: Living expenses (fixed + variable essentials); a fund of 3 to 6 months (13 to 26 weeks) of them; weeks to build, rounded up; saving first on payday; monitoring by variance (actual − budget) and its effect on the time to the target; choosing 3 or 6 months by how steady the income is. Closes the strand. Not: credit cards and loans (Year 12).
